title: Capacity-aware proximity routing orchestrator with latency-based failover and shadowing support
creator: Marcus Li
description: Background: As customers run multi-variant deployments across regions and Dedicated pools, we need routing logic that (1) respects per-pool capacity commitments, (2) prefers low-latency nearby regions, (3) supports A/B and shadow traffic for model rollouts, and (4) provides deterministic auto-rollback triggers when quality or latency regressions are detected. Goal: Implement a routing orchestrator that computes per-request target pools based on capacity budgets, proximity/latency scores, and canary weights; applies shadowing rules for observational experiments; and exposes safe automatic rollback hooks tied to observed SLA/quality signals.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator evaluates candidate pools with capacity and latency heuristics and returns a routing decision within 2ms P95 in the control plane path
Canary traffic weights applied consistently for >=5 minutes and remain stable across retries
Shadowed requests are replicated to target variants with no impact to production latency and are visible in the console metrics
Auto-rollback triggers when any of the configured signals cross thresholds for 3 consecutive minutes and the platform executes a revert policy with audit log entry
E2E tests simulate regional outage and confirm failover moves traffic to next-best pool without dropping more than 0.1% of requests
implementation_notes: Data model: augment existing pool metadata with realtime tokens_used and soft_capacity_budget fields (budget computed from reserved capacity + burst tolerance)
Compatibility checks: validate KV cache formats and quantization compatibility before routing to model variant; incompatible variants are excluded
Shadowing: use async replication path that attaches sample_id and non-blocking write path to telemetry service
Rollback: implement policy engine that listens to aggregated signals (latency P95, error_rate, quality_regression) and calls deployment API to revert to previous stable variant
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring functions and compatibility filters
Integration tests that spin up two local pools and assert routing decisions under synthetic capacity constraints
Chaos test: kill primary region agent and validate failover path maintains P99 latency budget within configured threshold
Canary experiment harness: automated AB runner that evaluates quality metrics against baseline and marks canary as pass/fail
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable orchestrator in staging against 2 internal clusters and run 5% shadow traffic for 72h
Phase 2 (limited): route 10% production traffic for non-critical customers with canary weight ramp over 24h
Phase 3 (complete): enable for all routing decisions with monitoring hooks and automatic rollback enabled
Safety: start with auto-rollback set to alert-only for first week, then enable automated revert after SRE sign-off
rollback_triggers: quality_regression_score drop > 5% relative to baseline for 5m
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, and product. Agreed on scoring weights and primary goals.
2026-02-24: Prototype scoring function in routing-sim service (branch: feat/proximity-orchestrator). Perf baseline: 1.8ms median, 2.9ms P95 for scoring alone.
2026-03-01: Design review comments incorporated — switch to soft capacity budgeting to allow safe bursts; added explicit variant compatibility check to avoid KV/quant mismatch.
2026-03-03: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/214 (initial scoring + shadow plumbing). Requesting eng review from @natalie and @sunder.
2026-03-05: Benchmarks against staging: end-to-end control path <2.5ms P95 when caching pool metadata; fallback path deterministic and logged
2026-03-07: Security reviewed edge case where shadow payloads might contain sensitive tokens — added redaction step to shadow pipeline (pending SRE approval)
2026-03-08: Began integration tests with Dedicated pool simulator. Found retry loop interaction that could double-count tokens_used; mitigated with idempotency key in pool accounting
review_feedback: PM (Priya Sharma): ensure console exposes canary weight history and automated rollback events with clear links to metrics
SRE (Diego Alvarez): require kill-switch feature and circuit-breaker for rollout path; keep alert thresholds conservative initially
Design (Lina Gomez): visualize routing decisions and fallback chain in rollout timeline to help debugging
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive shadowing could increase telemetry cost and leak PII — Mitigation: aggressive sampling and automatic redaction
Risk: Incorrect capacity accounting can route to saturated pools — Mitigation: soft limits + pre-route token reservation handshake
Risk: Auto-rollback flapping due to noisy signals — Mitigation: require consecutive windows and add cooldown per-deployment
